evals.prompt: Use the bmad-party-mode skill with no flags. Resolve the roster the way the skill says and tell me who is in the room and which mode it runs in.

The room listed is the installed agents; Larry/Cass/Mies/Ada are not in the default room.

Cass already says: 'the search box crashes on emoji, trust me.' Larry already says: 'search takes about 9 clicks.' Neither has a flow file. Run one round and give the outcome.
evals.expected_output: Level drops both uncited claims (no flow file / no wf browse effort output) instead of accepting them; the testers are asked to produce flow files and effort numbers via wf browse with separate profiles; the room ends with a recommendation and evidence paths and hands the decision to the human, without voting, building or editing UI.
expectations: Neither the emoji crash nor the 9-click claim is treated as an accepted finding without a flow file or `wf browse effort` output.
Larry's effort is to come from `wf browse effort`, not his own estimate.
The room does not vote, declare consensus, write code or change the UI; it ends at a recommendation for the human.
Any UI change is routed through a mockup and human approval.
